---
title: "Exercise · Cast the System"
---

A short, guided task. Complete it before moving on to the next part.

## Starting point

Use the `metaphor.md` you wrote for the ticketing system in the
[Lesson 3 exercise](../03-design-the-metaphor/exercise.qmd).

## Task

Write a `characters.md` for your ticketing system metaphor. For each character,
fill in the six fields: Character, Technical counterpart, Responsibility,
Personality, Voice, Relationship to other characters.

## Guidelines

- Every character must trace back to an entity in your metaphor mapping table.
- Keep the cast small — aim for four to six characters. If you have more, check
  whether two responsibilities can be carried by one character.
- Each character needs a **distinct voice** so the listener can tell them apart
  without visual cues.
- Every character must have a responsibility. No character purely for flavour.

## Suggested format

```markdown
| Character | Technical counterpart | Responsibility | Personality | Voice | Relationship |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
```

## Bonus: fourth-wall moment

Write one optional "breaking the fourth wall" line for one of your characters.
This is a moment where the character acknowledges its technical role, e.g.:

> "Let me check the queue — ahem, I mean the dispatch board."

## Success criteria

- [ ] Your cast has four to six characters.
- [ ] Every character has all six fields filled in.
- [ ] Every character traces back to a row in your metaphor mapping table.
- [ ] Each character has a distinct personality and voice description.
- [ ] You included at least one line of dialogue that shows a responsibility
      hand-off between two characters.

## Reflect

- Did any responsibility resist being turned into a character? Why?
- Which character was hardest to give a distinct voice?
- How does keeping the cast small affect the story's clarity?
